newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Metals - China sellers may stem zinc price rise.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals - China sellers may stem zinc price rise.

text.p: The current rally in the zinc market may be dampened by a return of Chinese sellers tempted by high prices, while aluminium and copper activity was lacklustre in Asia, traders said on Wednesday.
"While there is still room for zinc prices to move higher, I do not think the price hike would last with the Chinese likely to return to sell on current high levels," said a U.S trader.
"Chinese sellers may also want to get rid of any existing supplies ahead of the Chinese New Year holidays," he added.
The Chinese Lunar New Year begins on February 7 and could stretch up to 15 days in China.

Three month London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc prices hit a 10-month high on Tuesday following a 11,975-tonne fall in exchange stocks and the metal closed Tuesday's kerb trade $39 firmer at $1,109 a tonne.
At 0700 GMT on Wednesday, three month zinc was quoted at $1,105/$1,110 in Singapore.
A trader with a Japanese firm said he expected zinc prices to firm by a further $40 to $50 a tonne within the next two weeks as "fundamentals were strong".
But he added that the uptrend may be reversed near the end of January as high prices would attract sellers.
"I would like to keep my (zinc) stocks at the moment and see how prices are before selling them," said the trader.
Traders said both the copper and alumium markets were under pressure as China's ample stocks of both metals limited overall buying interest in the region.

"China is awash with metals and they are unlikely to import more as they have sufficient to tide them over the festive holidays during which all business would come to a standstill," said the U.S. trader.
He said this would dampen prices in the short term but the markets could attract some support after the Chinese return following the holiday period.
On copper, he said the market had lost its shine as prices failed to breach the $2,280 resistance level on the LME.
"Most people have left the copper market alone. While zinc trade dominates, copper levels have just drifted," said a Western trader.
Traders assessed support for three month LME copper between $2,220-$2,230 a tonne. Copper closed down at $2,261 on the exchange on Tuesday.
Cash copper was seen hovering around $2,418 a tonne at 0530 GMT on Wednesday.
Singapore copper premiums over LME cash prices were largely unchanged from last week and quoted at around $10-$20 a tonne by traders.
The volume of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse fell by 500 tonnes to 39,550 tonnes on Tuesay, down from 40,050 tonnes in the exchange's previous stocks report on January 10.
Traders said the aluminium market also showed signs of weakening. "The Chinese are expected to buy only after the Chinese New Year holidays," said the Japanese trader.
"The current sluggish Japanese economy has also dampened aluminium demand," he added.
